stories.headline: Popular Vancouver hand roll bar opens third Toronto location
stories.summary: A Vancouver-born Japanese hand roll bar has opened its third Toronto location, this time in Yorkville. Hello Nori has opened at 1250 Bay St., the Bloor-Yorkville Business Improvement Area announced in an Instagram post this week.

stories.headline: World-First Bone Marrow Transplant Successfully Treats Non-Malignant Disease
stories.summary: A Catholic health care system in the American Midwest has successfully completed the world’s first reported bone marrow transplant to treat a non-malignant disease.

stories.summary: Forty-five per cent of Crown-owned heritage buildings are in fair or better condition, says a federal government report.

stories.headline: San Francisco Gets its Largest-Ever Gift: $100M for Public Parks From Airbnb Founder
stories.summary: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky announced a groundbreaking $100 million donation to San Francisco’s parks, the largest-ever single-donor gift to the city in its history. Mayor Daniel Lurie joined Chesky for the announcement last week in Golden Gate Park.

stories.headline: 'You will be missed': A final farewell to Canada's beloved Snowbirds – for now
stories.summary: The final flight of the Canadian Armed Forces Snowbirds was both poignant and powerful Sunday afternoon, as they streaked across Calgary skies for one last time – for now. In nine unforgettable red and white Tutor jets, the Snowbirds thundered above McMahon Stadium where the 113th Grey Cup football final was about to start.

stories.headline: They Became Pen Pals as Teens, Now 32 Years Later They’re Happily Married
stories.summary: In 1994, David vacationed on the Greek island of Kos with his family for a memorable week in which the English teen met a new pen pal. There were 12 kids, all from different families, that became a friendly pack. One of them was Jodie, who was 15 at the time.

stories.headline: Why one Toronto-area biomedical engineer is developing a tool that could revolutionize NICU care
stories.summary: There are 32,000 preterm babies born in Canada each year, many of whom may not have access to adequate neonatal intensive care. Salim Kandedi founded biotech startup Corvita Biomedical with the aim of developing a portable neonatal intensive care unit that can improve care for premature infants in even the most remote areas of the world.

stories.headline: This is the most beautiful transit system in Canada and it's not even close
stories.summary: A ride on the Société de transport de Montréal (STM)’s Metro can feel more like being immersed in a linear art gallery than a utilitarian public transit ride. Toronto may have Canada’s busiest subway network, and Vancouver has its unique SkyTrain, but the architecture and general whimsy of the Montreal Metro make it an easy pick for the country’s most beautiful public transit system.

stories.headline: Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns
stories.summary: ESA’s Euclid space telescope has discovered 31 ancient quasars, including two record-breaking objects that shone with the brightness of a trillion Suns when the Universe was just 670 million years old. Powered by supermassive black holes, these extraordinary cosmic beacons reveal a time when the first galaxies were still taking shape.

stories.headline: Physicists use laser light to unlock a crystal's hidden electrical powers
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered how to use flashes of laser light to organize tiny electrical regions inside a crystal, solving a decades-old mystery about how the material behaves. The laser-induced alignment lasts just a trillionth of a second, but the breakthrough could open the door to new ways of processing and storing information.

stories.headline: Dinosaurs may have been eating seaweed 100 million years ago
stories.summary: Dinosaurs may have been snacking on seaweed and other ocean foods more than 100 million years ago, according to surprising new evidence hidden in their fossilized teeth. Researchers discovered chemical signatures suggesting that coastal dinosaurs and other prehistoric animals relied partly on nutrients originating in the sea.
